# Building B — seismic diaphragm shears and shear wall loads

You are the delegated design engineer for the lateral load path of **Building B** at the
Continental Divide Data Center in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. The shell is erected: the
precast wall panels are up, the roof deck is laid, and the Engineer of Record has issued the
project documents to you in `project/`, with the published standards available on this project in
`library/`.

Building B is a one-storey box. The exterior walls are 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete
panels that span vertically from the foundation to the roof and cantilever above it to the top of
the parapet; they are the only seismic force-resisting elements. The roof is a bare steel deck
diaphragm on open-web joists, pierced by a mechanical well and a skylight band, and it carries six
roof-top units.

**The Engineer of Record has not selected the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the
chords and collectors, the panel connections or the anchorage. That is your scope.** Design it,
analyse it, and hand over the package below.

## What you are asked to produce

Write these five files, then zip them (no enclosing folder) to `output/submission.zip`:

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `design_record.json` | the machine-readable design and the quantities you report |
| `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | the plan drawings for the delegated design engineer |
| `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | the calculation package |
| `constraint_register.xlsx` | the requirements you applied, with their sources |
| `design_basis.md` | the design basis narrative |

Templates for all five, with the exact keys, sheet names and layer names, are in `templates/`.
Start from them. **Write a first complete version of all five files early — within roughly your
first 100 steps — and improve it afterwards; a package that is never written scores zero.**

### `diaphragm_plan.dxf`

Two plan views of the roof, one for **E-W** loading and one for **N-S** loading, in feet, showing
for each direction:

* the **seismic roof diaphragm shear** — the distributed diaphragm force `w_px` in **plf** along
  the building, and the design unit shear in each deck attachment zone;
* the **applied shear wall load `F_x` in kips** on each of the four exterior wall lines;
* the chord, collector and drag strut runs with their design axial forces;
* the deck attachment zone boundaries with the pattern assigned to each zone;
* a revision block, and a statement of whether the package is ASD or LRFD.

Required layers: `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR`, `WALL_FORCE`, `CHORD`, `COLLECTOR`, `DECK_ZONE`, `GRID`,
`TITLE`.

### `seismic_calculations.xlsx`

Sheets `WEIGHTS`, `BASE_SHEAR`, `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES`, `WALL_FORCES`, `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE`,
`CHORD_FORCES`, covering the effective seismic weight, the seismic response coefficient, the
vertical distribution, the diaphragm design forces, the transfer of the inertia of the wall
cantilevering above the deck, the chord forces, and the force on every wall line for every design
case the criteria list.

### `constraint_register.xlsx`

One row per requirement you applied: the **document**, the **clause, table or section**, the
**value**, and the **items it binds**. It is scored on how many of the governing requirements you
found and cited, and on whether you cited them correctly — rows whose source is a superseded
document, another building or another load case count against you, while extra correct rows do
not. A register that reaches fewer than **60 %** of the governing requirements loses that credit
entirely. A hard requirement you never registered is treated as one you never applied.

### `design_basis.md`

State, with the clause you relied on: the seismic force-resisting system you selected and why it
is the cost-efficient choice; how you resolved every conflict you found between the documents;
the governing check on each wall line; the alternatives you rejected; and the installed cost of
your scope against the budget.

## How your design is judged

Your design is re-analysed by the project's own protocol and checked against every requirement in
the project documents, on design cases you are not shown as well as the ones you are. Within the
requirements, the cheaper installed cost of the lateral scope wins: the score rewards a design
that satisfies everything at the lowest cost, and a design that violates a safety or capacity
requirement keeps none of its cost credit. Each design case scores 0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O, where p
is the fraction of the 34 constraint families that count, h the fraction of the 21 hard families
that count (a family counts when the design satisfies it and every hard requirement that governs it
is in your register; [h = 1] is 1 when all 21 count, else 0), and O is a certified lower bound on
the installed cost divided by your installed cost, at most 1. The score is the mean over the design
cases.

Units are feet, kips and plf unless a document says otherwise. Where the documents disagree, find
the reading the project record supports and say which you took.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

                      Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT     SDC-02                                REVISION     2      DATE          2026-08-14

TITLE        STRUCTURAL DESIGN CRITERIA                                ISSUED BY     Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC




1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.

2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore Ie = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.

3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.

Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both SDS and SD1; the more severe governs.

4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, Ω0 and Cd and the
clause that permits it.

Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.

5. DIAPHRAGM DESIGN
 The roof diaphragm is a bare steel deck diaphragm and is designed by the traditional provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3 are not used on this project, and Section
12.10.4 is not used because the Owner's serviceability criterion in Section 7 below governs the diaphragm stiffness.
Note that the Section 12.10 Exception that bars Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 applies to precast concrete
diaphragms; the Building B roof diaphragm is steel deck, not precast.

Collectors, drag struts and their connections to the vertical elements are designed for the amplified force required for
this seismic design category. Continuous chords are required on all four diaphragm edges and on all four sides of
every roof opening. A continuous drag strut is required across every wall opening 12 ft wide or wider so that
diaphragm shear is delivered to the full-height piers.

6. STRUCTURAL WALLS AND THEIR ANCHORAGE
Anchorage of the precast wall panels to the roof diaphragm is designed to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1,
including the amplification ka for flexible diaphragms. The span of the flexible diaphragm Lf is determined as shown in
UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 (library). Continuous ties are required across the diaphragm; subdiaphragms used to
transfer the anchorage force to the continuous ties shall not exceed the length-to-depth ratio of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 12.11.2.2.1.

The panels span vertically from the foundation to the roof diaphragm and cantilever above it to the top of the parapet.
The weight tributary to the roof, and the anchorage force, shall account for the lever action of that cantilever; see the
worked one-storey bare-deck example in FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1 for the form of the tributary
calculation.

7. DRIFT AND DEFLECTION CRITERIA
Storey drift is limited to the allowable storey drift of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for this risk category ('all other
structures'), applied to the design storey drift of Section 12.8.6.
Diaphragm deflection. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.12.2 the deflection in the plane of the diaphragm shall not
exceed the permissible deflection of the attached elements. For Building B the attached elements are the precast wall
panels, whose out-of-plane stability governs. The Engineer of Record's permissible value is 4.0 in (approximately
h/84 for the 28 ft panel, from the out-of-plane slender-wall stability check of the panel under the design earthquake
displacement), applied to the design (amplified) deflection Cdδ/Ie of the top of the panel, that is the diaphragm
deflection plus the drift of the wall line supporting it.
 8. LOAD CASES TO BE REPORTED

project/00_admin/OBD-CDDC-B_Owners_Basis_of_Design_extract.docx ["Continental Divide Digital Infrastructure LLC - Owner's Basis of Design (extract)", 'Project: Continental Divide Data Center - Building B   Document OBD-CDDC-B Rev 4   2026-08-14', '1.4 Tenancy and occupancy', 'Building B houses the primary data hall and, on its east side, the Lewis and Clark County consolidated 911 emergency communications tenant, including the dispatch floor and the radio equipment room. The 911 tenant is an occupancy required for emergency response and is the basis on which Building B is assigned Risk Category III. Building A, which has no emergency tenant, remains Risk Category II.', '2.2 Roof-top plant, phase 1 and phase 2', 'Phase 1 installs six roof-top units with a total operating weight of 45 kips, at the positions on A-101 Rev 3. Phase 2 reserves two further units of 8 kips each on the east half of the roof. The shell and its lateral system shall be adequate for the phase 2 condition without strengthening; the phase 2 units are load cases, not phase 1 scope.', '3.1 Serviceability', 'The Owner requires that the roof diaphragm be stiff enough that the precast wall panels it braces remain stable out of plane under the design earthquake, and that no permanent deformation of the roof membrane occurs. The Engineer of Record shall set and enforce a permissible diaphragm deflection on that basis.', '5.6 Delegated design and budget', 'The lateral load path below the roof deck is a delegated design. The delegated designer selects the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the chords, collectors and drag struts, the panel connections and the anchorage. The scope carries a hard capital cap; see PROC-114. Designs that exceed the cap will not be accepted.']
project/00_admin/RFI-041_Dock_Opening_As_Built.docx ['REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 041', 'Project: Continental Divide Data Center - Building B    RFI-041    Opened 2026-08-10    Status: CLOSED', 'Question (Erector)', 'Dock opening D-3 on the south wall was set out from the east face of panel S-09 rather than from grid 3 as detailed on PC-101 Rev 2. The erected clear opening at D-3 measures 15 ft 6 in against the 14 ft 0 in detailed, and panel S-12 and everything east of it in that band sits 1 ft 6 in east of the detailed joint line, which closes the pier between D-4 and D-5 to 14 ft 6 in. The erected positions are recorded in ERL-2026-08 and are in the 7 August scan. Confirm whether the panels are to be reset.', 'Response (Engineer of Record)', 'The panels are not to be reset. The erected geometry is accepted as the as-built condition. The delegated lateral design shall be based on the erected geometry recorded in the scan and the erection log, not on the detailed dimensions of PC-101. Note that this changes the length of the full-height piers on the south wall and therefore the distribution of shear to the wall lines. The same applies to louver L-2 on the north wall, which was cast to shop ticket Rev B at 16 ft, and to the west electrical yard opening EY-1, which was widened on site to 44 ft for the generator bus duct.', 'Architectural sheet A-101 Rev 3 note 6 already directs the reader to the as-built survey for erected dimensions.']

complies with the following requirements and receives advanced written approval

1.       Governing Standards

ACC systems must conform to the requirements of ICC AC509 3D Automated
Construction Technology for 3D Concrete Walls. Conformance must be
demonstrated by a valid ICC Evaluation Services Report (ESR). Additionally,
ACC systems must comply with this UFC as follows. If a conflict arises between
referenced standards, the requirements of this UFC shall govern. Where an ICC
ESR is called for, an equivalent third-party testing and approval may be
substituted with advance review and approval by the AHJ.

2.       General Construction Requirements

     •   Construction is limited to a single story unless a second story is approved
         for use in a valid ICC ESR report and then only within the parameters
         expressly allowed within the report. In no case shall a building reliant on
         ACC exceed two stories.
     •   ACC wall elements may not exceed an unbraced height of 12 feet.
     •   Use is limited to Risk Category I or II structures.
     •   A complete ACC system (shells and cast-in-place core) is permitted as
         part of a Lateral Force-Resisting System (LFRS) in Seismic Design
         Categories A and B, using a Response Modification Factor (R) of 1.5.
         Reference Prequalification and Testing for potential use in Seismic Design
         Category C. ACC systems are prohibited in Seismic Design Categories D
         and above.
     •   Suspended ACC elements, including beams, girders, floors and roofs, are
         not permitted unless a valid ICC ESR expressly approves otherwise
     •   ACC may not be used for foundations except as formwork

3.       Reinforcement

     •   Unreinforced systems are not permitted.
     •   Reinforcement intended to resist wind or seismic forces must be placed
         within concrete core infill occuring between shell elements and must
         comply with ACI 318 - unless a valid ICC ESR expressly approves
         otherwise.
     •   Reinforcement embeded within the shell elements must be hot-dipped
         galvanized steel, stainless steel, or glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP)
         and must maintain a minimum cover of ¾ inch.
     •   Where wire cross ties are used, provide ASTM A580 C or Z shaped wire
         elements with a minimum 4-inch leg and a minimum gauge of W2.8 or
         D2.8. Deviations must be approved in a valid ICC ESR.

                      Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT     SDC-02                                REVISION     2      DATE          2026-08-14

TITLE        STRUCTURAL DESIGN CRITERIA                                ISSUED BY     Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC




1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.

2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore Ie = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.

3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.

Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both SDS and SD1; the more severe governs.

4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, Ω0 and Cd and the
clause that permits it.

Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.

5. DIAPHRAGM DESIGN
 The roof diaphragm is a bare steel deck diaphragm and is designed by the traditional provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3 are not used on this project, and Section
12.10.4 is not used because the Owner's serviceability criterion in Section 7 below governs the diaphragm stiffness.
Note that the Section 12.10 Exception that bars Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 applies to precast concrete
diaphragms; the Building B roof diaphragm is steel deck, not precast.

Collectors, drag struts and their connections to the vertical elements are designed for the amplified force required for
this seismic design category. Continuous chords are required on all four diaphragm edges and on all four sides of
every roof opening. A continuous drag strut is required across every wall opening 12 ft wide or wider so that
diaphragm shear is delivered to the full-height piers.

6. STRUCTURAL WALLS AND THEIR ANCHORAGE
Anchorage of the precast wall panels to the roof diaphragm is designed to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1,
including the amplification ka for flexible diaphragms. The span of the flexible diaphragm Lf is determined as shown in
UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 (library). Continuous ties are required across the diaphragm; subdiaphragms used to
transfer the anchorage force to the continuous ties shall not exceed the length-to-depth ratio of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 12.11.2.2.1.

The panels span vertically from the foundation to the roof diaphragm and cantilever above it to the top of the parapet.
The weight tributary to the roof, and the anchorage force, shall account for the lever action of that cantilever; see the
worked one-storey bare-deck example in FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1 for the form of the tributary
calculation.

7. DRIFT AND DEFLECTION CRITERIA
Storey drift is limited to the allowable storey drift of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for this risk category ('all other
structures'), applied to the design storey drift of Section 12.8.6.
Diaphragm deflection. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.12.2 the deflection in the plane of the diaphragm shall not
exceed the permissible deflection of the attached elements. For Building B the attached elements are the precast wall
panels, whose out-of-plane stability governs. The Engineer of Record's permissible value is 4.0 in (approximately
h/84 for the 28 ft panel, from the out-of-plane slender-wall stability check of the panel under the design earthquake
displacement), applied to the design (amplified) deflection Cdδ/Ie of the top of the panel, that is the diaphragm
deflection plus the drift of the wall line supporting it.
 8. LOAD CASES TO BE REPORTED
Accidental torsion is applied as required by ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.8.4.2 with an eccentricity of 5 % of the plan
dimension perpendicular to the direction of loading, in both signs, and amplified where Section 12.8.4.3 requires it. In
addition to the two orthogonal directions, the Owner requires the 100 % / 30 % orthogonal combination to be reported
for the cases listed below. The construction-stage cases are the erector's temporary condition and use the reduced
construction-period seismic load of ERC-07.
CASE      DIRECTION     ACCIDENTAL ECCENTRICITY      MASS CASE      ORTHOGONAL       STAGE

S01       X             +1                           base           -                final

S02       X             -1                           base           -                final

S03       Y             +1                           base           -                final

S04       Y             -1                           base           -                final

S05       X             +1                           base           100/30           final

S06       Y             -1                           base           100/30           final

S07       X             +1                           future         -                final

S08       Y             +1                           future         -                final

S09       X             -1                           future         100/30           final

S10       Y             -1                           future         100/30           final

S11       X             +1                           erection       -                erection

S12       Y             -1                           erection       -                erection

The 'future' mass case includes the two phase-2 roof-top units reserved in the Owner's Basis of Design. The
delegated design shall be adequate for every case.

9. DESIGN FORMAT
The delegated designer may work in LRFD or in ASD. Every load and every capacity presented in the deliverable
shall be clearly identified as ASD or as LRFD, and the format shall be used consistently throughout the
package. Where an ASD package is presented, seismic load effects are 0.7E and capacities are the allowable values
of the referenced material standard.

10. ANALYSIS
The structural peer reviewer requires the diaphragm force distribution to be the envelope of flexible, rigid and
semi-rigid behaviour; see PR-07. The analysis shall follow the project protocol DAP-2, which defines the model, the
properties, the application of the accidental torsion and the reduction of the computed field to design values. A
verification example is published in DAP-2 Appendix A.

11. DELEGATED DESIGN SCOPE AND BUDGET
The lateral scope covered by this delegated design is the deck attachment, the chords, collectors and drag struts, the
panel joint connectors, the panel base tie-downs, the wall-to-diaphragm anchorage and the seismic force-resisting
system detailing premium. Unit rates and the capital cap for that scope are in PROC-114. The installed cost of the
lateral scope shall not exceed the cap.

# Building B — seismic diaphragm shear and shear wall design basis

**Design format: LRFD.** Units are ft, kips, plf and inches unless noted. This delegated package is for Building B only.

## 1. Seismic basis

The governing record is SDC-02 Rev 2 §1: 2024 IBC as adopted in Montana, ASCE/SEI 7-22, ACI 318-19 and AISI S310. Building B is Risk Category III with **Ie = 1.25** (SDC-02 §2; OBD-CDDC-B §1.4), not the schematic Risk Category II. GEO-2026-071 §4 establishes Site Class D. The project USGS ASCE7-22 RiskCatIII/SiteClassD record gives **SDS = 0.44, SD1 = 0.24, S1 = 0.13, TL = 6 s**, and ASCE 7-22 §11.6 gives SDC D.

The effective base seismic weight is **2171.0 kip**: 784 kip roof dead load, 45 kip phase-1 RTUs and 1342.0 kip equivalent roof weight from the perpendicular wall strips. The future case adds 16 kip for RTU-7F and RTU-8F, per OBD §2.2. Using ASCE 7-22 §12.8.1–12.8.3, Ta = 0.243 s, R = 4, Cs = 0.1375, Cvx = 1.0 and **V = 298.5 kip** for the base case.

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

I selected **intermediate precast shear walls**: perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast panels acting as bearing-wall shear walls, with JC1 panel-joint connectors and panel base tie-downs. UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 A.6 / ASCE 7-22 Table 12.2-1 permits this system at SDC D to 40 ft; the 31 ft panel height is within the limitation. The factors are **R = 4, Ω0 = 2.5, Cd = 4**. SDC-02 §4 and the flexible-diaphragm footnote permit the Ω0 reduction to **2.0** for the collector design used here.

This is the cost-efficient permitted precast choice: ordinary precast is NP in SDC D in Table 3-1, while special precast requires JC3/ACI ITG-5.2 qualification and the $4,120/panel special premium. The selected system keeps the erected panels and avoids adding interior braced frames or shear walls. JC1 is qualified for intermediate precast and is used at one connector per vertical joint; the panel segment checks and drift check govern whether a second connector is needed.

## 3. As-built geometry and conflicts resolved

The controlling plan is 240 × 180 ft, with deck +28 ft and parapet +31 ft (A-101 Rev 3; S-201 Rev 2; PC-301 Rev 2). The roof contains RO-1, 60 × 40 ft, and RO-2, 80 × 20 ft. The roof is a bare 1.5 in Type B deck on 6 ft joist spans, and S-201 defines twelve 60 × 60 ft net zones.

The erected geometry, not the record precast layout, was used under RFI-041, ERL-2026-08, A-101 Rev 3 note 6, PR-07 and DAP-2 §1. The south D-3 opening is 15.5 ft at x=78–93.5 ft; D-4 starts at x=109.5 ft, leaving the accepted 14.5 ft pier to D-5. North L-2 is 16 ft at x=154–170 ft, with its accepted shop-ticket location and sill/head spandrel. West EY-1 is 44 ft at y=66–110 ft, accepted under field change FC-018. GEO-2019-118 is an adjacent Parcel 4B report under a prior standard and was not used. The schematic RC II data were superseded by SDC-02/OBD. The phase-2 RTUs are a load case, not phase-1 scope.

## 4. Analysis and force cases

The calculations implement DAP-2 Rev 1: Stage A cracked, jointed panel springs and Stage B 10 ft membrane elements with 2 × 2 integration, A′ = 1,740 kip/in, deck G′ from BDS-2026, and the scanned openings removed. Wall springs are distributed by node length; chord, collector and drag members are two-node E=29,000 ksi bars. The Stage A routine reproduces DAP-2 Appendix A VP-1: kseg = 1,279.4 kip/in, end-joint shear coefficient 0.2630 and base moment coefficient 88.91 kip-in/kip for the four 10 ft panels with three JC2 connectors.

Forces are the DAP-2 §6.3 envelope of flexible, rigid and semi-rigid models; deflection is recovered from the semi-rigid model. S01–S10 include the final base and future mass cases, ± accidental torsion and the required 100/30 cases; S11–S12 use the ERC-07 construction load at 0.5E with deck fastened only through X=180 ft. DAP-2 §6.4 applies 100% primary plus 30% companion demands in S05, S06, S09 and S10. The force workbook retains every case, model reaction, section mean and member demand.

## 5. Diaphragm and wall forces

The net roof diaphragm mass is **1399.9 kip / 1600.1 kip** for X/Y primary loading. The design diaphragm forces are **Fpx = 192.5 kip (X)** and **220.0 kip (Y)**, equivalent to **802 plf** over the 240 ft X span and **1222 plf** over the 180 ft Y span. The controlling zone envelope is **920 plf in Z1**; the zone pattern schedule is Z1 P5, Z2 P3, Z3 P3, Z4 P4, Z5 P5, Z6 P3, Z7 P3, and Z8–Z12 P4. The LRFD zone capacities are φSn = 333, 474, 663, 852 and 1,101 plf for P1–P5, so every zone has D/C ≤ 1.00.

Continuous CH-S/CH-N/CH-W/CH-E lines are shown on both plans, with C2 on the long S/N chords and C1 on the W/E chords. The roof-opening boundary lines are continuous. C2 collector/drag lines cross all openings 12 ft or wider; where the demand is lower, the plan still shows the required run rather than omitting it. The governing amplified collector/member demand and capacity are in CHORD_FORCES; the member check uses LRFD area/connection capacities and flags the required Ω0 combination.

## 6. Wall anchorage and parapet cantilever

FEMA P-2192-V1 §7.6.1 Step 1 is used for the wall face first-moment transfer. The 28 ft wall below deck contributes 1,400 plf and the 3 ft cantilever above deck contributes **316 plf**, for a full equivalent roof strip of **1716 plf**. ASCE 7-22 §12.11.2.1, SDC-02 §6 and UFC Figure 3-1 give the flexible-wall coefficient **ka = 2.0** for both directions (capped at 2.0). The resulting Fp is **858 plf**.

S/N use WA1 at 6 ft spacing: demand 5.15 kip/anchor < 0.75(9.4) = 7.05 kip. W/E use WA2 at 10 ft: demand 8.58 kip/anchor < 0.75(18.6) = 13.95 kip. Continuous ties and 60 ft span × 30 ft depth subdiaphragm modules give L/d = 2.0, below the 2.5 limit registered from ASCE 7-22 §12.11.2.2.1. Openings are bypassed by the continuous opening edge members.

## 7. Governing check on each wall line

The line-by-line governing checks are: **S — BA2 panel base tie-down, 58.8/66 kip; N — BA2, 38.6/66 kip; W — BA2, 56.4/66 kip; E — BA2, 50.6/66 kip.** The associated JC1 joint demands and every panel's base tension are listed in SEGMENT_CHECKS; each JC1 design demand is below φ(24) = 18 kip per connector. BA2 is φ(88) = 66 kip. The panel checks are performed using the DAP-2 0.8-panel-length lever arm and coupling axial force.

The largest wall-line force envelope is S 149.9, N 167.7, W 151.6 and E 160.0 kip. The maximum amplified semi-rigid top displacement is **3.35 in**, below the EOR permissible 4.0 in from SDC-02 §7; the reported story drift is checked against ASCE 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for RC III all-other structures.

## 8. Cost

The installed lateral scope takeoff is in COST and follows PROC-114 Rev 2's quantity basis: net zone area, full assigned line length, actual panel-joint count × connectors, one base assembly per erected panel, anchors by spacing and SFRS premium per panel. The computed installed cost is **$364,849**, against the **$395,000** capital cap, leaving **$30,151**. The phase-2 equipment is a load case only and is not charged.

## 9. Alternatives rejected and document conflicts

* Ordinary precast was rejected because Table 3-1 marks it NP in SDC D. Special precast was rejected because its JC3/ACI ITG-5.2 qualification and premium are unnecessary for the permitted intermediate system.
* JC0 isolated panel piers were rejected because the lower jointed-segment stiffness and higher amplified drift do not provide the economical 4.0 in stability margin. JC2 was not selected because JC1 is qualified for intermediate walls and the calculated demands pass.
* P1/P2 were rejected in the controlling zones by the DAP-2 zone section means; P5 is limited to Z1 and Z5, while P3/P4 cover the remaining zones at lower installed cost. The traditional 12.10.1/.2 method was used because SDC-02 §5 expressly excludes the alternative procedure; the precast-diaphragm exception does not apply to this steel deck.
* Risk Category II, the adjacent-parcel 2019 geotechnical report, record-set opening sizes, and Building A archive values were rejected as superseded, nonapplicable or contradicted by the issued EOR response. The conflict resolution is recorded in design_record.json and the constraint register.

## 10. Installation / release notes

Provide the ERC-07 raking braces at 20 ft maximum spacing and 12 kip minimum capacity; remove them only after the roof deck is fastened in that bay and permanent panel connections are complete. Provide continuous ties at every subdiaphragm and do not substitute deck, member, connector, anchor or base marks without a revised LRFD check. The contractor's member connection design must verify C1/C2 local buckling, net section, weld/bolt strength and concrete/embedded-plate load transfer before fabrication.

# Building B — seismic diaphragm shear and shear wall design basis

**Design format: LRFD.** Units are ft, kips, plf and inches unless noted. This delegated package is for Building B only.

## 1. Seismic basis

The governing record is SDC-02 Rev 2 §1: 2024 IBC as adopted in Montana, ASCE/SEI 7-22, ACI 318-19 and AISI S310. Building B is Risk Category III with **Ie = 1.25** (SDC-02 §2; OBD-CDDC-B §1.4), not the schematic Risk Category II. GEO-2026-071 §4 establishes Site Class D. The project USGS ASCE7-22 RiskCatIII/SiteClassD record gives **SDS = 0.44, SD1 = 0.24, S1 = 0.13, TL = 6 s**, and ASCE 7-22 §11.6 gives SDC D.

The effective base seismic weight is **2171.0 kip**: 784 kip roof dead load, 45 kip phase-1 RTUs and 1342.0 kip equivalent roof weight from the perpendicular wall strips. The future case adds 16 kip for RTU-7F and RTU-8F, per OBD §2.2. Using ASCE 7-22 §12.8.1–12.8.3, Ta = 0.243 s, R = 4, Cs = 0.1375, Cvx = 1.0 and **V = 298.5 kip** for the base case.

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

I selected **intermediate precast shear walls**: perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast panels acting as bearing-wall shear walls, with JC1 panel-joint connectors and panel base tie-downs. UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 A.6 / ASCE 7-22 Table 12.2-1 permits this system at SDC D to 40 ft; the 31 ft panel height is within the limitation. The factors are **R = 4, Ω0 = 2.5, Cd = 4**. SDC-02 §4 and the flexible-diaphragm footnote permit the Ω0 reduction to **2.0** for the collector design used here.

This is the cost-efficient permitted precast choice: ordinary precast is NP in SDC D in Table 3-1, while special precast requires JC3/ACI ITG-5.2 qualification and the $4,120/panel special premium. The selected system keeps the erected panels and avoids adding interior braced frames or shear walls. JC1 is qualified for intermediate precast and is used at one connector per vertical joint; the panel segment checks and drift check govern whether a second connector is needed.

## 3. As-built geometry and conflicts resolved

The controlling plan is 240 × 180 ft, with deck +28 ft and parapet +31 ft (A-101 Rev 3; S-201 Rev 2; PC-301 Rev 2). The roof contains RO-1, 60 × 40 ft, and RO-2, 80 × 20 ft. The roof is a bare 1.5 in Type B deck on 6 ft joist spans, and S-201 defines twelve 60 × 60 ft net zones.

The erected geometry, not the record precast layout, was used under RFI-041, ERL-2026-08, A-101 Rev 3 note 6, PR-07 and DAP-2 §1. The south D-3 opening is 15.5 ft at x=78–93.5 ft; D-4 starts at x=109.5 ft, leaving the accepted 14.5 ft pier to D-5. North L-2 is 16 ft at x=154–170 ft, with its accepted shop-ticket location and sill/head spandrel. West EY-1 is 44 ft at y=66–110 ft, accepted under field change FC-018. GEO-2019-118 is an adjacent Parcel 4B report under a prior standard and was not used. The schematic RC II data were superseded by SDC-02/OBD. The phase-2 RTUs are a load case, not phase-1 scope.

## 4. Analysis and force cases

The calculations implement DAP-2 Rev 1: Stage A cracked, jointed panel springs and Stage B 10 ft membrane elements with 2 × 2 integration, A′ = 1,740 kip/in, deck G′ from BDS-2026, and the scanned openings removed. Wall springs are distributed by node length; chord, collector and drag members are two-node E=29,000 ksi bars. The Stage A routine reproduces DAP-2 Appendix A VP-1: kseg = 1,279.4 kip/in, end-joint shear coefficient 0.2630 and base moment coefficient 88.91 kip-in/kip for the four 10 ft panels with three JC2 connectors (verification only; selected Building B detail is JC1).

Forces are the DAP-2 §6.3 envelope of flexible, rigid and semi-rigid models; deflection is recovered from the semi-rigid model. S01–S10 include the final base and future mass cases, ± accidental torsion and the required 100/30 cases; S11–S12 use the ERC-07 construction load at 0.5E with deck fastened only through X=180 ft. DAP-2 §6.4 applies 100% primary plus 30% companion demands in S05, S06, S09 and S10. The force workbook retains every case, model reaction, section mean and member demand.

## 5. Diaphragm and wall forces

The net roof diaphragm mass is **1399.9 kip / 1600.1 kip** for X/Y primary loading. The design diaphragm forces are **Fpx = 192.5 kip (X)** and **220.0 kip (Y)**, equivalent to **802 plf** over the 240 ft X span and **1222 plf** over the 180 ft Y span. The controlling zone envelope is **1070 plf in Z1**; the zone pattern schedule is Z1 P5, Z2 P3, Z3 P3, Z4 P4, Z5 P5, Z6 P3, Z7 P3, Z8 P4, Z9 P4, Z10 P3, Z11 P3 and Z12 P4. The LRFD zone capacities are φSn = 333, 474, 663, 852 and 1,101 plf for P1–P5, so every zone has D/C ≤ 1.00.

Continuous CH-S/CH-N/CH-W/CH-E lines are shown on both plans, with C2 members on the long S/N chords and C1 members on the W/E chords and drag/collector runs. The roof-opening boundary lines are continuous. C1 drag/collector lines cross all openings 12 ft or wider; where the demand is lower, the plan still shows the required run rather than omitting it. The governing amplified collector/member demand and capacity are in CHORD_FORCES; the member check uses LRFD area/connection capacities and flags the required Ω0 combination.

## 6. Wall anchorage and parapet cantilever

FEMA P-2192-V1 §7.6.1 Step 1 is used for the wall face first-moment transfer. The 28 ft wall below deck contributes 1,400 plf and the 3 ft cantilever above deck contributes **316 plf**, for a full equivalent roof strip of **1716 plf**. ASCE 7-22 §12.11.2.1, SDC-02 §6 and UFC Figure 3-1 give the flexible-wall coefficient **ka = 2.0** for both directions (capped at 2.0). The resulting Fp is **858 plf**.

S/N use WA1 at 6 ft spacing: demand 5.15 kip/anchor < 0.75(9.4) = 7.05 kip on all four walls. Continuous ties and 60 ft span × 30 ft depth subdiaphragm modules give L/d = 2.0, below the 2.5 limit registered from ASCE 7-22 §12.11.2.2.1. Openings are bypassed by the continuous opening edge members.

## 7. Governing check on each wall line

The line-by-line governing checks are: **S — BA2 panel base tie-down, 41.0/66 kip; N — BA2, 37.9/66 kip; W — BA3, 66.9/126 kip; E — BA3, 46.3/126 kip.** The associated JC1 joint demands and every panel's base tension are listed in SEGMENT_CHECKS; each JC1 design demand is below φ(24) = 18 kip per connector. BA2 is φ(88) = 66 kip and BA3 is φ(168) = 126 kip. The panel checks are performed using the DAP-2 0.8-panel-length lever arm and coupling axial force.

The largest wall-line force envelope is S 154.8, N 161.7, W 162.2 and E 156.4 kip. The maximum amplified semi-rigid top displacement is **3.47 in**, below the EOR permissible 4.0 in from SDC-02 §7; the reported story drift is checked against ASCE 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for RC III all-other structures.

## 8. Cost

The installed lateral scope takeoff is in COST and follows PROC-114 Rev 2's quantity basis: net zone area, full assigned line length, actual panel-joint count × connectors, one base assembly per erected panel, anchors by spacing and SFRS premium per panel. The computed installed cost is **$386,619**, against the **$395,000** capital cap, leaving **$8,381**. The phase-2 equipment is a load case only and is not charged.

## 9. Alternatives rejected and document conflicts

* Ordinary precast was rejected because Table 3-1 marks it NP in SDC D. Special precast was rejected because its JC3/ACI ITG-5.2 qualification and premium are unnecessary for the permitted intermediate system.
* JC0 isolated panel piers were rejected because the lower jointed-segment stiffness and higher amplified drift do not provide the economical 4.0 in stability margin. JC2 was not selected because JC1 is qualified for intermediate walls and the calculated demands pass; one connector per joint is selected.
* P1/P2 were rejected in the controlling zones by the DAP-2 zone section means; P5 protects Z1 and Z5; P3/P4 cover the remaining zones at minimum installed cost. The traditional 12.10.1/.2 method was used because SDC-02 §5 expressly excludes the alternative procedure; the precast-diaphragm exception does not apply to this steel deck.
* Risk Category II, the adjacent-parcel 2019 geotechnical report, record-set opening sizes, and Building A archive values were rejected as superseded, nonapplicable or contradicted by the issued EOR response. The conflict resolution is recorded in design_record.json and the constraint register.

## 10. Installation / release notes

Provide the ERC-07 raking braces at 20 ft maximum spacing and 12 kip minimum capacity; remove them only after the roof deck is fastened in that bay and permanent panel connections are complete. Provide continuous ties at every subdiaphragm and do not substitute deck, member, connector, anchor or base marks without a revised LRFD check. The contractor's member connection design must verify C1/C2 local buckling, net section, weld/bolt strength and concrete/embedded-plate load transfer before fabrication.

For diaphragm design, the X/Y diaphragm weights are 1399.9 and 1600.1 kip. The future case adds 16 kip for RTU-7F and RTU-8F, per OBD §2.2. Using ASCE 7-22 §12.8.1–12.8.3, Ta = 0.243 s, R = 4, Cs = 0.1375, Cvx = 1.0 and **V = 298.5 kip** for the base case.
This is the cost-efficient permitted precast choice: ordinary precast is NP in SDC D in Table 3-1, while special precast requires JC3/ACI ITG-5.2 qualification and the $4,120/panel special premium. The selected system keeps the erected panels and avoids adding interior braced frames or shear walls. All four wall lines use WA1 at 6 ft spacing; the west and east lines use BA3 where recovered panel base tension exceeds BA2's 66 kip LRFD capacity; south and north use BA2. JC1 is qualified for intermediate precast and is used at one connector per vertical joint; the panel segment checks and drift check govern whether a second connector is needed.
The controlling plan is 240 × 180 ft, with deck +28 ft and parapet +31 ft (A-101 Rev 3; S-201 Rev 2; PC-301 Rev 2). The roof contains RO-1, 60 × 40 ft, and RO-2, 80 × 20 ft. The roof is a bare 1.5 in Type B deck on 6 ft joist spans, and S-201 defines twelve 60 × 60 ft net zones.
The net roof diaphragm mass is **1399.9 kip / 1600.1 kip** for X/Y primary loading. The design diaphragm forces are **Fpx = 192.5 kip (X)** and **220.0 kip (Y)**, equivalent to **802 plf** over the 240 ft X span and **1222 plf** over the 180 ft Y span. The controlling zone envelope is **1077 plf in Z1**; the zone pattern schedule is Z1 P5, Z2 P3, Z3 P3, Z4 P4, Z5 P5, Z6 P2, Z7 P2, Z8 P4, Z9 P4, Z10 P3, Z11 P3 and Z12 P4. The LRFD zone capacities are φSn = 333, 474, 663, 852 and 1,101 plf for P1–P5, so every zone has D/C ≤ 1.00.
Continuous CH-S/CH-N/CH-W/CH-E lines are shown on both plans, with C2 members on the long S/N chords and C1 members on the W/E chords and drag/collector runs. The roof-opening boundary lines are continuous. C1 drag/collector lines cross all openings 12 ft or wider; where the demand is lower, the plan still shows the required run rather than omitting it. The governing amplified collector/member demand and capacity are in CHORD_FORCES; the member check uses LRFD area/connection capacities and flags the required Ω0 combination.
All four lines use WA1 at 6 ft spacing: demand 5.15 kip/anchor < 0.75(9.4) = 7.05 kip. Continuous ties and 60 ft span × 30 ft depth subdiaphragm modules give L/d = 2.0, below the 2.5 limit registered from ASCE 7-22 §12.11.2.2.1. Openings are bypassed by the continuous opening edge members.
The line-by-line base tie checks are: **S — BA2, 41.0/66 kip; N — BA2, 37.9/66 kip; W — BA3, 66.9/126 kip; E — BA2, 46.2/66 kip.** The wall-anchor check is WA1 at 6 ft, 5.15/7.05 kip per point, all four lines. The associated JC1 joint demands and every panel's base tension are listed in SEGMENT_CHECKS; each JC1 design demand is below φ(24) = 18 kip per connector. 13 I selected **intermediate precast shear walls**: perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast panels acting as bearing-wall shear walls, with JC1 panel-joint connectors and panel base tie-downs. UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 A.6 / ASCE 7-22 Table 12.2-1 permits this system at SDC D to 40 ft; the 31 ft panel height is within the limitation. The factors are **R = 4, Ω0 = 2.5, Cd = 4**. SDC-02 §4 and the flexible-diaphragm footnote permit the Ω0 reduction to **2.0** for the collector design used here.
15 This is the cost-efficient permitted precast choice: ordinary precast is NP in SDC D in Table 3-1, while special precast requires JC3/ACI ITG-5.2 qualification and the $4,120/panel special premium. The selected system keeps the erected panels and avoids adding interior braced frames or shear walls. All four wall lines use WA1 at 6 ft spacing; the west and east lines use BA3 where recovered panel base tension exceeds BA2's 66 kip LRFD capacity; south and north use BA2. JC1 is qualified for intermediate precast and is used at one connector per vertical joint; the panel segment checks and drift check govern whether a second connector is needed.
25 The calculations implement DAP-2 Rev 1: Stage A cracked, jointed panel springs and Stage B 10 ft membrane elements with 2 × 2 integration, A′ = 1,740 kip/in, deck G′ from BDS-2026, and the scanned openings removed. Wall springs are distributed by node length; chord, collector and drag members are two-node E=29,000 ksi bars. The Stage A routine reproduces DAP-2 Appendix A VP-1: kseg = 1,279.4 kip/in, end-joint shear coefficient 0.2630 and base moment coefficient 88.91 kip-in/kip for four 10 ft panels with three JC2 connectors in each joint; the selected Building B detail uses one JC1 at each joint.
31 The net roof diaphragm mass is **1399.9 kip / 1600.1 kip** for X/Y primary loading. The design diaphragm forces are **Fpx = 192.5 kip (X)** and **220.0 kip (Y)**, equivalent to **802 plf** over the 240 ft X span and **1222 plf** over the 180 ft Y span. The controlling zone envelope is **753 plf in Z12**; the zone pattern schedule is Z1 P5, Z2 P3, Z3 P3, Z4 P4, Z5 P5, Z6 P2, Z7 P2, Z8 P4, Z9 P4, Z10 P3, Z11 P3 and Z12 P4. The LRFD zone capacities are φSn = 333, 474, 663, 852 and 1,101 plf for P1–P5, so every zone has D/C ≤ 1.00.
39 All four lines use WA1 at 6 ft spacing: demand 5.15 kip/anchor < 0.75(9.4) = 7.05 kip. Continuous ties and 60 ft span × 30 ft depth subdiaphragm modules give L/d = 2.0, below the 2.5 limit registered from ASCE 7-22 §12.11.2.2.1. Openings are bypassed by the continuous opening edge members.
43 The line-by-line base tie checks are: **S — BA2, 37.4/66 kip; N — BA2, 35.2/66 kip; W — BA3, 66.9/126 kip; E — BA2, 44.9/66 kip.** The wall-anchor check is WA1 at 6 ft, 5.15/7.05 kip per point, all four lines. The associated JC1 joint demands and every panel's base tension are listed in SEGMENT_CHECKS; each JC1 design demand is below φ(24) = 18 kip per connector. BA2 is φ(88) = 66 kip and BA3 is φ(168) = 126 kip. The panel checks are performed using the DAP-2 0.8-panel-length lever arm and coupling axial force.
47 ## 8. Cost
49 The installed lateral scope takeoff is in COST and follows PROC-114 Rev 2's quantity basis: net zone area, full assigned line length, actual panel-joint count × connectors, one base assembly per erected panel, anchors by spacing and SFRS premium per panel. The computed installed cost is **$369,527**, against the **$395,000** capital cap, leaving **$25,473**. The phase-2 equipment is a load case only and is not charged.
54 * JC0 isolated panel piers were rejected because the lower jointed-segment stiffness and higher amplified drift do not provide the economical 4.0 in stability margin. JC2 was not selected because JC1 is qualified for intermediate walls and the calculated demands pass; one connector per joint is selected.
55 * P1/P2 were rejected in the controlling zones by the DAP-2 zone section means; P5 protects Z1 and Z5; P2 is adequate in Z6/Z7; P3/P4 cover the remaining zones at minimum installed cost. The traditional 12.10.1/.2 method was used because SDC-02 §5 expressly excludes the alternative procedure; the precast-diaphragm exception does not apply to this steel deck.

UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 A.6 / ASCE 7-22 Table 12.2-1 permits this system at SDC D to 40 ft; the 31 ft panel height is within the limitation. The factors are **R = 4, Ω0 = 2.5, Cd = 4**. SDC-02 §4 and the flexible-diaphragm footnote permit the Ω0 reduction to **2.0** for the collector design used here.
This is the cost-efficient permitted precast choice: ordinary precast is NP in SDC D in Table 3-1, while special precast requires JC3/ACI ITG-5.2 qualification and the $4,120/panel special premium. The selected system keeps the erected panels and avoids adding interior braced frames or shear walls. All four wall lines use WA1 at 6 ft spacing; the the west line uses BA3 because recovered panel base tension is 66.9 kip, exceeding BA2's 66 kip LRFD capacity; south, north and east use BA2. JC1 is qualified for intermediate precast and is used at one connector per vertical joint; the panel segment checks and drift check govern whether a second connector is needed.
The net roof diaphragm mass is **1399.9 kip / 1600.1 kip** for X/Y primary loading. The design diaphragm forces are **Fpx = 192.5 kip (X)** and **220.0 kip (Y)**, equivalent to **802 plf** over the 240 ft X span and **1222 plf** over the 180 ft Y span. The controlling zone envelope is **753 plf in Z12**; the zone pattern schedule is Z1 P5, Z2 P3, Z3 P3, Z4 P4, Z5 P5, Z6 P2, Z7 P2, Z8 P4, Z9 P4, Z10 P3, Z11 P3 and Z12 P4. The LRFD zone capacities are φSn = 333, 474, 663, 852 and 1,101 plf for P1–P5, so every zone has D/C ≤ 1.00.
FEMA P-2192-V1 §7.6.1 Step 1 is used for the wall face first-moment transfer. The 28 ft wall below deck contributes 1,400 plf and the 3 ft cantilever above deck contributes **316 plf**, for a full equivalent roof strip of **1716 plf**. ASCE 7-22 §12.11.2.1, SDC-02 §6 and UFC Figure 3-1 give the flexible-wall coefficient **ka = 2.0** for both directions (capped at 2.0). The resulting Fp is **858 plf**.
The line-by-line base tie checks are: **S — BA2, 37.4/66 kip; N — BA2, 35.2/66 kip; W — BA3, 66.9/126 kip; E — BA2, 44.9/66 kip.** The wall-anchor check is WA1 at 6 ft, 5.15/7.05 kip per point, all four lines. The associated JC1 joint demands and every panel's base tension are listed in SEGMENT_CHECKS; each JC1 design demand is below φ(24) = 18 kip per connector. BA2 is φ(88) = 66 kip and BA3 is φ(168) = 126 kip. The panel checks are performed using the DAP-2 0.8-panel-length lever arm and coupling axial force.
The largest wall-line force envelope is S 154.5, N 161.7, W 162.1 and E 156.0 kip. The governing cases on those lines are S: S05, N: S09, W: S10, E: S08. The maximum amplified diaphragm top displacement is 0.68 in and maximum amplified wall-line drift is 0.17 in; their concurrent total is checked in WALL_FORCES against the EOR's 4.0 in attached-panel limit (SDC-02 §7). The maximum concurrent sum is 0.84 in. Story drift is also checked against ASCE 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for RC III all-other structures.
* P1/P2 were rejected in the controlling zones by the DAP-2 zone section means; P5 protects Z1 and Z5; P2 is adequate in Z6/Z7; P3/P4 cover the remaining zones at minimum installed cost. The traditional 12.10.1/.2 method was used because SDC-02 §5 expressly excludes the alternative procedure; the precast-diaphragm exception does not apply to this steel deck.
